decisions.claim: B is looking for a room at a motel
decisions.reason: Turn 3 explicitly offers B the last room, presupposing B is seeking a room at the motel.
Definite possessive 'your car' in turn 11 presupposes B has a car.
Turn 13 explicitly addresses B as 'sir', directly stating the form of address and implying male.

decisions.claim: B is checking in and receiving a room key
decisions.reason: Turn 11 'Here is your key' explicitly shows B receiving a key as part of check-in.

decisions.claim: B is staying at the motel
decisions.reason: 'Enjoy your stay with us' in turn 13 presupposes B will be staying at the motel.
c3 already captures 'addressed as sir (male)' which is the more complete form; c6 is a weaker projection of the same evidence.

decisions.claim: B received a key to room 56 at the motel
decisions.reason: Second-review support: Turn 5 explicitly identifies the room being discussed as 'number 56 at the rear of the motel.' Turn 11 hands B 'your key' and then says 'You can park your car in front of our room,' where 'our room' is anaphorically linked to the only room described in the conversation (room 56). The entire dialogue is a single check-in transaction for that specific room. While the key handover sentence doesn't restate '56,' the discourse structure makes the referent unambiguous: there is only one room under discussion, identified as 56 in turn 5, and the key in turn 11 is for it. This is a definite possessive ('your key') in context establishing B's receipt of the key for room 56.
decisions.counterexample: If the conversation had introduced multiple rooms or if the key handover were separated by a topic shift to a different room, the link would be weaker. Here, no such shift occurs.

decisions.claim: B arrived at the motel seeking a room and was offered the last available room

decisions.claim: B's assigned room has two double beds

decisions.claim: B's room is at the rear of the motel
decisions.reason: Turn 5 states the room is 'number 56 at the rear of the motel', describing the room being offered to B.

decisions.claim: The room B is staying in costs forty-five dollars a night for two
